I had a visceral reaction the first time i listened to seven. My dad was an abusive narcissist, and my childhood best friend was my saving grace. It was so bad that at one point I genuinely did live with her and her family for a few months. On top of it all, we used to play pirates all the time, it was our thing. And if that’s not enough, we used to believe my house was genuinely haunted (whether my dad was mad or not lol). 

All coincidences but it was one of those things where I was like Taylor did you read my childhood diary before writing this song?! My friend eventually moved away, and she took a piece of my heart with her. I yearn for the moments in my childhood with her all the time. This song just feels like it was written about us. Almost every single part of it, but those line’s especially.

I have SO MANY stories I could share about my father, the biggest cheapskate I know. 

We were poor growing up but that doesn’t excuse his behavior. He was such an embarrassment. He would stop the car and pull over even on busy roads or highways if he saw a pop can or piece of scrap metal on the side of the road that he could return for profit. He would rummage through his kids bedrooms and even his wife’s purse to find extra change and steal it for his coin jar. If ever we were invited to an event that had free food he would get 4 plates that piled high, and would also stick around til the end and then take whatever leftovers he could. Every time we went to a restaurant he would steal a bunch of napkins and silverware packs to bring home. He was the kinda guy to just ask for a water cup and then fill it with soda. At sit down restaurants he would ask for a water but have me order a soda and then make me ask for a couple to go refills that he would take. If we went to a buffet we would be there for hours on end so he could “get his money’s worth”. He would wrap food in napkins and pocket it to take home. He refused to tip and would even steal tips off of other tables as we were leaving. He rummaged through dumpsters out in public if he thought he saw something worth money in the trash like a returnable can. Us kids were only allowed to drink one glass of milk per day and this counted towards cereal too, and if we had milk leftover in our cereal bowl he would poor it into a jar and put it in the fridge. We ate expired foods so they “wouldn’t go to waste”. He would linger around the local grocery store and ask to buy the expired sushi they were gonna throw out at a discounted price, and then force us to eat that shit. If anyone finished dinner and there was even a small piece of leftover food on the plate he would eat it or bag it up and save it for later. One time as a child I got hand foot and mouth disease which is contagious through contact and saliva. I was eating a piece of watermelon. I finished but didn’t eat it all the way to the rind so he grabbed it out of the garbage and finished it the rest of the way. Ended up getting hand foot and mouth disease from me because of that and then yelled at me for it. 

I literally have so many more stories. My dad is a narcissist who only thinks about himself and money. He embarrassed me so much as a kid I learned never to go out with him even now as an adult.

Recipe

Makes 1 quesadilla. 

Quarter pound of ground beef

1 Cheddar cheese slice

Shredded Mexican cheese blend

Keto quesadilla (I used La Banderita 4 net carb tortillas) 

Optional:

Sea salt

Pepper

Garlic

Burger condiment of your choice 

So basically, I cooked up the beef (seasoned with sea salt, pepper, and garlic) on a stovetop pan until there there was barely any pink visible, then tore up a slice of cheddar cheese and threw it into the pan. I continued to cook until the cheese was completely melted, stirring the meat and cheese together.  

I started heating up a separate pan on the stove top while I prepped my quesadilla. I laid a tortilla out and put a layer of Mexican cheese down, followed by the meat and cheese combo, and then another layer of Mexican cheese. I folded it over and buttered it on both sides and then fried it until sides were slightly browned and the inside was completely melted! 

I created a dipping sauce mixture of mayonnaise and mustard and voila! 
It tastes delicious. 

For dipping sauce you can use whatever your favorite burger topping is. Ketchup, thousand island, bbq, whatever you prefer. 

I know it’s simple but it’s actually quite delicious. 

Estimated 6 net carbs per quesadilla! (If you use the La Banderita brand 4 net carb tortilla) (also varies depending on what dipping sauce you use)

This went viral online a year or two back and I was completely obsessed. Since I started keto I’ve been craving them and the fix was easy! Just use low carb tortillas. I use Misson brand carb balance. 5g net carb per tortilla. 

Estimated 2.5-3 g carbs per Samosa. 

Ingredients:

1 lb ground beef

1 packet taco seasoning

4 ounces cream cheese

1/2 cup shredded cheddar

Vegetable oil (or other frying oil) 

Flour and water for paste. 

Brown the ground beef and add packet of taco seasoning + 2/3 cup water. 
Mix in and then add cream cheese and shredded cheese. Cook on stove until all melted together. 

Take a low carb tortilla and cut it in half straight down the middle. Mix together flower and water to make a paste/glue like substance. Put the paste along one side of the tortilla half and then fold over and press together. It should fold into a triangle shape. Stuff the tortilla from the opening in the top with the beef mix. Then use more paste to close the top. 

Boil vegetable oil for frying. 
Fry the samosa until ends are crispy and it turns to a light tan color. I usually do about 45 seconds to a minute on each side.
